name: SIM900A GSM / GPRS
summary: 2G GSM/GPRS modem controlled with AT commands.
caution: Requires a dedicated burst-current-rated supply, compatible SIM/antenna and confirmed local 2G service; verify UART logic levels.
whatIs: A second-generation (2G) cellular modem that exchanges SMS, calls or GPRS data using AT commands over a serial interface.
howTo: Identify the exact SIM900A breakout power input, UART levels, antenna connector and SIM requirements.
Prepare a dedicated, burst-current-capable supply; do not power the modem from an Arduino GPIO pin.
Choose the selected board's compatible serial port and cross-connect TX to RX only after verifying voltage compatibility.
Open a serial terminal, send AT and check for an OK response; test network registration only when 2G coverage is confirmed.
suggestedLibraries: Arduino HardwareSerial or SoftwareSerial on a suitable AVR board
firstExperiment: Read the modem model and basic AT response.

name: SIM800L GSM
summary: Common 2G GSM modem controlled through AT commands.
caution: Do not assume 5V supply or MCU GPIO power. Carrier 2G coverage and exact breakout requirements must be checked.
whatIs: A small 2G cellular modem often used for SMS and data applications; it is not compatible with 4G-only service.
howTo: Read the specific SIM800L board's supply range and peak current requirements before attaching power.
Install a suitable cellular antenna and active SIM with confirmed local 2G support.
Use a board-appropriate UART and verified level shifting where needed.
Run a minimal AT response test, then check SIM/network registration separately.
suggestedLibraries: Board UART; optional TinyGSM for advanced network examples
firstExperiment: Receive AT/OK without attempting SMS.

name: SIM7600 4G LTE
summary: Cellular LTE modem family; supported bands and board connections vary by region and variant.
caution: Check exact SIM7600 variant, cellular bands, antenna and dedicated supply; not a drop-in SIM900 replacement.
whatIs: A family of LTE cellular modem modules with USB and serial control interfaces; available frequency bands depend on the variant.
howTo: Identify the exact SIM7600 suffix and verify the cellular bands and SIM with your carrier.
Choose the vendor's documented supply, antenna arrangement and USB/UART level requirements.
Connect a compatible USB host or dedicated serial port using the exact breakout pinout.
Read modem identification and registration status before attempting data access.
suggestedLibraries: Vendor AT reference; optional TinyGSM after matching modem support
firstExperiment: Identify the modem firmware/version using AT commands.

name: NEO-6M GPS
summary: Receives GPS navigation data, commonly via NMEA serial messages.
caution: NEO-6 is an older module family. Breakout supply levels differ from bare IC ratings; GPS fix needs an antenna and satellite visibility.
whatIs: A GPS receiver that processes satellite signals and sends navigation messages, commonly as NMEA sentences on UART.
howTo: Inspect the antenna and breakout label to confirm supply and serial logic levels.
Connect receiver TX to the MCU UART RX with compatible levels; a TX-to-receiver-RX connection is optional for basic reading.
Use the matching board serial port and, if desired, TinyGPSPlus to decode NMEA messages.
Test outdoors with a clear sky view; show both valid and no-fix states rather than inventing coordinates.
suggestedLibraries: TinyGPSPlus for parsing; a serial monitor can display raw NMEA
firstExperiment: Print whether a valid location fix has been acquired.

name: NEO-M8N GNSS
summary: Multi-constellation GNSS receiver family used in navigation applications.
caution: Verify exact module interface, firmware, antenna and board supply before designing connections.
whatIs: A multi-constellation GNSS receiver family for position, time and speed measurements.
howTo: Identify the exact breakout model and available UART, I2C or USB interface.
Check supply and antenna requirements and connect only voltage-compatible pins.
Read receiver messages with the supported interface or a manufacturer tool.
Confirm fix status in an open-sky location before using coordinates.
suggestedLibraries: TinyGPSPlus for supported NMEA UART output
firstExperiment: Display satellite/fix status, not fabricated locations.

name: HC-05 Bluetooth
summary: Bluetooth Classic serial transceiver commonly controlled through UART.
caution: Confirm 3.3V UART levels on the specific board; do not confuse Bluetooth Classic with BLE.
whatIs: A Bluetooth Classic Serial Port Profile module, commonly used to bridge a microcontroller UART and another Bluetooth device.
howTo: Check the HC-05 module's power supply, logic levels and mode pins on the specific breakout.
Connect UART TX/RX appropriately, using level shifting if required for the module RX.
Start a simple UART echo sketch with a documented baud rate.
Pair with a compatible Bluetooth Classic device and verify a text exchange; BLE-only devices may not work.
firstExperiment: Echo a short text message over Bluetooth Classic.

name: nRF24L01 2.4 GHz RF
summary: Common 2.4 GHz packet-radio transceiver module.
caution: Check its 3.3V supply and decoupling; never connect 5V logic to a non-tolerant SPI module.
whatIs: A 2.4 GHz packet radio transceiver that communicates with a microcontroller over SPI.
howTo: Use a verified 3.3V power source and place recommended local decoupling near the transceiver.
Identify the board's valid SPI and CE/CSN GPIO pins using its schematic.
Install an appropriate RF24 library and connect two compatible transceivers.
Send numbered packets between devices and report actual acknowledgements or packet loss.
firstExperiment: Send a test counter between two radios.

name: SX1278 / RA-02 LoRa
summary: LoRa radio transceiver used for long-range low-data-rate communication.
caution: Use region-appropriate permitted frequencies, a suitable antenna and compatible 3.3V power/logic.
whatIs: A LoRa radio transceiver module controlled via SPI for low-data-rate wireless links.
howTo: Verify the exact module, regional permitted frequency, antenna and 3.3V voltage requirements.
Connect MOSI/MISO/SCK, chip select, reset and interrupt pins based on the selected MCU board.
Use a maintained SX127x-compatible LoRa library and set a region-appropriate frequency.
Exchange test messages between two devices with correct antennas; measure real reception rather than assuming range.
suggestedLibraries: LoRa or RadioLib library (verify compatibility first)
firstExperiment: Exchange a labeled test message between two LoRa nodes.

name: MFRC522 RFID reader
summary: 13.56 MHz RFID reader module used for reading supported tags.
caution: Check radio protocol, tags, power and SPI logic; RFID IDs alone are not secure authentication.
whatIs: A 13.56 MHz RFID reader IC often found on RC522 SPI breakout boards.
howTo: Check that the RC522 breakout receives the appropriate low-voltage supply and GPIO levels.
Connect SPI pins and reader reset/SS to known usable GPIOs.
Install a matching MFRC522 reader library for the selected board.
Read a compatible tag's UID and confirm that a UID alone is not secure access authentication.
firstExperiment: Read and print the UID of a test RFID tag.

name: PN532 NFC / RFID
summary: NFC reader/controller module supporting multiple communication interfaces.
caution: Select and verify the breakout's hardware interface, supply and available libraries.
whatIs: An NFC controller chip used for supported proximity-card and NFC communications.
howTo: Identify whether the breakout is configured for I2C, SPI or UART and its allowed supply voltage.
Select the matching interface and verify its board wiring.
Install the compatible PN532 library and run a reader-detection example.
Scan a supported test tag and handle unsupported tag types without assumptions.
firstExperiment: Detect a supported NFC tag without writing to it.

name: BME280 environment sensor
summary: Sensor family for temperature, humidity and pressure measurements.
caution: BME280 and BMP280 are not identical; verify breakout marking, I2C address and voltage levels.
whatIs: A digital environmental sensor that measures temperature, humidity and atmospheric pressure.
howTo: Check the actual BME280 marking; avoid confusing it with BMP280, which has no humidity measurement.
Power the breakout within its specified range and connect I2C/SPI at safe logic levels.
Find the I2C address or chosen SPI pins and install a compatible BME280 library.
Read temperature, humidity and pressure; compare with a known reference for sanity checking.
suggestedLibraries: Adafruit BME280 and Adafruit Unified Sensor
firstExperiment: Show temperature, humidity and pressure on Serial Monitor.

name: BMP280 pressure sensor
summary: Sensor family for pressure and temperature measurements.
caution: Do not expect humidity readings; verify actual module variant and breakout voltage regulator.
whatIs: A pressure and temperature sensor; unlike BME280 it does not directly measure humidity.
howTo: Confirm the breakout is BMP280, not BME280 or a different compatible-looking sensor.
Verify breakout supply, I2C/SPI voltage and address selection.
Use the matching BMP280 library and read pressure and temperature.
Show measured values and flag read failures rather than assuming correct calibration.
suggestedLibraries: Adafruit BMP280 and Adafruit Unified Sensor
firstExperiment: Display pressure and temperature.

name: MPU-6050 IMU
summary: Motion sensor with acceleration and gyroscope measurements.
caution: Confirm address selection, voltage tolerance and orientation calibration before use.
whatIs: A six-axis inertial measurement unit containing an accelerometer and gyroscope.
howTo: Confirm the breakout's supply and I2C address pin configuration.
Wire a compatible I2C bus and use board-correct SDA/SCL connections.
Install a supported MPU6050 library and read raw acceleration/rotation.
Calibrate offsets with the sensor stationary, then rotate the module to observe changes.
firstExperiment: Detect a tilt or angular-rate change.

name: DS18B20 temperature
summary: Digital temperature sensor used on a one-wire data bus.
caution: Verify sensor authenticity, wiring mode, pull-up and supply voltage; water resistance depends on probe assembly.
whatIs: A digital temperature sensor that communicates over a one-wire bus.
howTo: Identify the probe or bare sensor pinout and choose powered or parasite-power mode.
Use a proper pull-up resistor on the data line as specified for the chosen topology.
Install OneWire and DallasTemperature libraries and scan the sensor address.
Read a temperature, check disconnected-sensor errors and compare against a reference.
firstExperiment: Read one sensor without treating -127°C as real data.

name: MAX30102 optical pulse sensor
summary: Optical heart-rate sensing component sometimes included in hobby breakout modules.
caution: Educational estimates are not medical measurements; verify board voltage, optical layout and signal conditioning.
whatIs: An optical photoplethysmography sensor component used for experimental pulse-signal monitoring.
howTo: Check the exact breakout's regulator and level-shifter arrangement before connecting I2C.
Follow the vendor's mechanical/optical setup and select a compatible driver library.
Read raw red/infrared samples while the sensor is uncovered, then with a finger positioned consistently.
Plot the raw waveform and clearly label any derived pulse value as non-medical.
firstExperiment: Plot relative optical signal values; no clinical diagnosis.

name: ADS1115 16-bit ADC
summary: External analog-to-digital converter useful for low-voltage measurements.
caution: Inputs must remain within the converter's supply and absolute ratings; never measure high voltage directly.
whatIs: A 16-bit analog-to-digital converter with a configurable gain setting that communicates over I2C.
howTo: Verify the ADS1115 board supply voltage and the maximum allowed analog pin range.
Connect I2C safely and start with a low-voltage, ground-referenced signal only.
Install a suitable ADS1X15 library and select the correct input and gain.
Read raw ADC counts and converted voltages; never exceed the ADC input supply or absolute ratings.
firstExperiment: Measure a known low-voltage divider output.

name: INA219 power monitor
summary: Shunt-based voltage/current monitor family for DC circuits.
caution: Check common-mode voltage, shunt selection, ground and current direction before designing power systems.
whatIs: A DC shunt-based current and bus-voltage monitor controlled over I2C.
howTo: Read the exact breakout shunt value, voltage range and layout.
Place the shunt in series only with a safely isolated, low-voltage DC test load.
Connect SDA/SCL and use a matching INA219 library.
Calibrate or verify using a multimeter and compare positive/negative current signs.
firstExperiment: Log DC load current and bus voltage under a safe test load.

name: INA226 voltage/current monitor
summary: Digital current/voltage/power monitor for shunt-based DC measurement.
caution: Verify bus voltage, common-mode range, shunt resistor and calibration; not directly suitable for mains.
whatIs: A precision shunt-based DC current, voltage and power monitor accessed through I2C.
howTo: Check allowed bus voltage, common-mode limits, the shunt value and wiring orientation.
Place the current shunt on the correct DC circuit path; avoid mains or unprotected high energy sources.
Connect the I2C bus and configure calibration using a suitable INA226 library.
Compare logged bus voltage/current against calibrated instruments before computing energy.
firstExperiment: Display measured DC current, voltage and calculated power.

name: SSD1306 OLED 128x64
summary: Monochrome OLED controller often used with Arduino graphics libraries.
caution: I2C address, driver variant, pull-ups and breakout voltage capabilities must be verified.
whatIs: A monochrome OLED display controller often used for 128×64 pixel graphics.
howTo: Confirm the OLED controller, pixel size and whether the breakout uses I2C or SPI.
Check the board supply, pull-ups, interface and address, commonly discovered by an I2C scanner.
Install Adafruit SSD1306 and Adafruit GFX libraries (or another compatible pair).
Render a simple text/rectangle demo and investigate blank display or wrong address errors.
suggestedLibraries: Adafruit SSD1306 and Adafruit GFX Library
firstExperiment: Show a hello message and a simple geometric shape.

name: LCD1602 I2C display
summary: Character LCD using an I2C expander backpack.
caution: The backpack's address, chip and LCD voltage vary; confirm PCF8574 variant and pull-up levels.
whatIs: A 16-character by 2-line LCD, often used with an I2C GPIO-expander backpack.
howTo: Identify the backpack's I2C expander and power supply requirements.
Use an I2C address scanner and connect board-correct SDA/SCL lines.
Install the hd44780 I2C-expander library or a verified compatible driver.
Print text on both lines and adjust the LCD contrast potentiometer if the screen is blank.
firstExperiment: Display two lines of sensor status text.

name: MCP2515 CAN controller
summary: Standalone CAN controller typically connected to an external CAN transceiver.
caution: CAN electrical bus requires an appropriate transceiver and termination; controller alone is insufficient.
whatIs: A stand-alone CAN bus controller that requires a separate CAN physical-layer transceiver.
howTo: Identify the MCP2515 oscillator frequency, transceiver type and breakout's supply/logic levels.
Connect MCU SPI, chip-select and interrupt pins from the chosen board schematic.
Fit bus termination and proper transceiver wiring for a safe, low-voltage test CAN network.
Configure a matching CAN library and verify receiving/sending frames on two nodes.
firstExperiment: Transmit a frame between two safely terminated CAN nodes.

name: MAX485 RS-485
summary: Differential serial transceiver for half-duplex RS-485 networks.
caution: Check bus termination, biasing, direction control, grounding and device variant logic levels.
whatIs: An RS-485 transceiver chip for converting UART-level serial signals into a differential pair.
howTo: Verify the exact breakout's supply and logic voltage; not every MAX485 variant works at 3.3V.
Connect UART TX/RX and direction pins, and route A/B over a suitable pair of wires.
Apply termination/biasing only as required by the bus topology.
Exchange a known packet with a second RS-485 device before adding Modbus framing.
firstExperiment: Receive a known serial packet across a short RS-485 link.

name: HC-SR04 ultrasonic distance
summary: Time-of-flight ultrasonic distance module with trigger and echo signals.
caution: Many 5V versions output a 5V echo; use level shifting when connecting to 3.3V GPIO.
whatIs: A pulse-echo ultrasonic distance module used for approximate object-range detection.
howTo: Identify the ultrasonic module voltage, trigger and echo labels.
Provide its documented supply and level-shift a 5V echo before any 3.3V GPIO.
Generate a short trigger pulse and time the echo with a timeout to avoid hanging.
Convert echo time to approximate distance, noting target shape and temperature affect accuracy.
firstExperiment: Measure an object at two known distances.

name: DHT22 / AM2302
summary: Low-cost temperature/humidity sensor family with a dedicated digital protocol.
caution: DHT11 and DHT22 have different performance; confirm the module supply and data pull-up.
whatIs: A digital sensor for approximate temperature and relative humidity readings.
howTo: Identify whether the sensor is DHT11, DHT22 or an AM2302 breakout, and verify pin order.
Connect a suitable supply and data pull-up when needed for the sensor wiring.
Install DHT sensor library with its required Unified Sensor dependency.
Sample at the sensor's recommended interval and check for invalid/NaN readings.
suggestedLibraries: DHT sensor library and Adafruit Unified Sensor
firstExperiment: Print temperature and humidity once every few seconds.

name: MQ-series gas sensors
summary: Heated semiconductor gas sensors used for approximate educational indications.
caution: Not calibrated life-safety alarms. Sensor heater requires power; outputs, warm-up and calibration differ by MQ type.
whatIs: MQ-series gas sensors use a heated sensing element and require careful calibration for meaningful results.
howTo: Identify the exact MQ model and its target-gas sensitivity before selecting a sample project.
Supply the heater and analog interface as specified; check voltage divider and ADC limits.
Log analog values and allow the manufacturer's recommended warm-up period.
Compare relative readings in controlled, safe conditions; do not use the DIY build as a gas-safety alarm.
suggestedLibraries: Analog input / ADC (no special library required)
firstExperiment: Observe changes in raw analog response, without inferring safety concentrations.

name: DS3231 RTC
summary: Battery-backed I2C real-time clock often used for logging and scheduled control.
caution: Confirm backup-cell chemistry, I2C address and board voltage/pull-up behavior.
whatIs: A high-accuracy battery-backed real-time clock accessed over I2C.
howTo: Identify I2C pins and the breakout's supply and pull-up voltages.
Verify backup-battery compatibility and safe charging-circuit design on the breakout.
Install RTClib and read current clock registers.
Set the RTC once, disconnect main power briefly, then verify it retained time.
firstExperiment: Show a stable timestamp before and after a power cycle.

name: MicroSD SPI module
summary: Removable microSD storage for logging sensor measurements.
caution: Check 3.3V card interface, module level shifting, CS pin and filesystem robustness.
whatIs: A microSD breakout provides removable storage, typically over SPI, for data logs.
howTo: Check whether the module includes appropriate regulation and signal level shifting.
Connect SPI pins and a suitable chip-select GPIO for the board.
Use the Arduino SD library or a board-compatible filesystem library.
Write a short CSV entry, close the file, and read the contents back to verify.
firstExperiment: Append and read a CSV row on a test microSD card.

name: L298N dual H-bridge driver
summary: Dual H-bridge for brushed DC motors or bipolar steppers.
caution: Motor power, thermal dissipation, back-EMF and separate MCU supply require engineering review.
whatIs: A dual H-bridge motor driver used to switch and reverse suitable DC motors.
howTo: Read the motor and driver voltage/current/thermal limitations; use a separate rated motor supply.
Connect logic inputs and enable pins according to the module schematic; share reference ground where appropriate.
Start with a small low-voltage motor, no mechanical load, and a current-limited supply.
Run forward/stop/reverse tests with safe pauses and check driver temperature.
suggestedLibraries: Arduino GPIO and PWM (no mandatory library)
firstExperiment: Reverse a small motor at low voltage while monitoring current.

name: Hobby servo motor
summary: Position or continuous-rotation hobby servos depending on the exact model.
caution: Do not assume continuous-rotation servos are position-controllable; use a separate appropriately sized supply.
whatIs: A hobby servo uses pulse timing to command position or speed depending on its design.
howTo: Identify whether the exact servo is standard positional or continuous rotation.
Use a separately sized regulated supply; never power a high-current servo from a GPIO.
Connect only a suitable control pin and common signal reference after verifying requirements.
Run a slow small-range test with a compatible servo library and watch for stalls.
suggestedLibraries: Servo on AVR; ESP32Servo on supported ESP32 variants
firstExperiment: Sweep a positional servo slowly, or test neutral/speed on continuous rotation.

name: Relay module 5V
summary: Electromechanical relay breakouts for electrically isolated switching.
caution: Verify input activation polarity, coil current, isolation and contact ratings. Avoid mains projects in Studio.
whatIs: A relay module uses a coil-driven switch to control an electrically separate circuit.
howTo: Identify module coil voltage, trigger polarity and optocoupler isolation arrangement.
Power coils from a suitable supply and verify the module's control input compatibility.
Begin with only a low-voltage, current-limited load; do not use mains wiring in Studio.
Toggle the relay under controlled conditions and inspect the contact's normally open/closed behavior.
firstExperiment: Toggle an LED on a separate low-voltage test circuit.
